name: Brahma Temple (Jagatpita Shri Brahma Mandir)
priceNote: free entry; photography banned inside; no dedicated paid shoe cloakroom confirmed
why: The reason Pushkar exists as a pilgrimage town. One of a small handful of temples in India dedicated to Brahma (not literally the world's only one, despite the common tourist-guide claim) and the most prominent one. Marble courtyard, worth an early or late visit to dodge tour buses.
warn: Midday closure 1:30-3:00pm is the detail most tourist pages omit or get wrong (some say 2-4pm instead). Hours shift to 6:30am-8:30pm in winter. No photography inside.

name: Savitri Mata Temple
priceNote: free; donation box at the shrine
why: Brahma's consort's hilltop shrine on Ratnagiri hill; the real draw is the 360-degree view over Pushkar Lake and the desert, repeatedly called the single best viewpoint in Pushkar, not overrated. Reachable by ~650-1200 stone steps (source step counts disagree) or the ropeway.
warn: No official gate-hours source found for the shrine itself - it's an open-air hilltop temple, visited whenever there's daylight. Ropeway opens 7:30am, which misses the ~6:00-6:10am September sunrise entirely, so walking is the only way to catch sunrise here.

name: Pushkar Ropeway (Savitri Mata Ropeway)
priceNote: one-way; return fare separately reported anywhere from INR 125-200 depending on source. Ride is 6-7 minutes each way. Prices and hours are NOT consistent across sources - see warn.
why: The lazy way up Ratnagiri hill to Savitri Mata Temple, 6-7 minutes each way versus a 30-45 minute climb. Sane choice for a sunset visit or to avoid the climb in heat.
warn: Three sources give three different operating windows: 7:30am-8:00pm, 7:00am-12:00pm plus 3:30-7:00pm (with a midday break), and 8:00am-6:00pm. This was flagged unresolved in the prior research pass and remains unresolved here - confirm at the counter on arrival, do not plan a tight schedule around a specific closing time. Whatever the window, it opens too late for September sunrise (~6:00-6:10am) - walk up instead if sunrise is the goal.

name: Gayatri Temple (Pap Mochani Mata)
priceNote: free
why: Smaller hilltop shrine to Brahma's other consort, on the opposite hill from Savitri - less touristed, still a real viewpoint over the town and lake.
warn: No midday closure reported for this one, unlike Brahma/Rangji/Varaha - treat as continuously open in the stated window, but this is an absence of evidence, not a confirmed absence of closure.

name: Rangji Temple
priceNote: temple free; small in-temple museum charges INR 5
why: South Indian Dravidian-gopuram-style temple in the middle of the bazaar - visually the odd one out among Pushkar's Rajasthani-style temples. Khichdi prasad around 8am, tamarind rice prasad around 8pm.
warn: This dataset could not verify a distinct 'old Rangji Temple' and 'new Rangji Temple' as two separate sites despite that being how the brief described it - only one Rangji Temple complex turned up in sources. Treat as one temple until confirmed on the ground.

name: Varaha Temple
priceNote: free (not separately confirmed but no source states a fee)
why: Pushkar's oldest surviving shrine (original construction ~1123-1150 AD), dedicated to Vishnu's boar avatar; demolished and rebuilt at least three times through history (Ghaznavi, then Aurangzeb, then Jai Singh II).
warn: Longest midday closure of any temple in this dataset - a full 4 hours, noon to 4pm. Easy to miss this window and find it shut.

name: Apteshwar Mahadev Temple
priceNote: free
why: 19th-century Shiva temple directly on the lake edge, close to Brahma Temple, with a five-faced white marble Mahadev murti. Easy to combine with the lakeside walk since it's only ~600m from Brahma Temple.
warn: No midday closure reported for this specific temple, which is unusual against the pattern of the others nearby - flagged as possibly just undocumented rather than confirmed absent.

name: Man Mahal
priceNote: no entry fee found; now operates as an RTDC-run heritage hotel (branded Hotel Sarovar) so paid access may depend on being a guest
why: Royal guest house built by Maharaja Man Singh I (1590-1614 AD) for his trips to Pushkar, on the lake edge in Rajasthani architectural style. Now a Rajasthan Tourism Development Corporation heritage hotel.
warn: Because it's a working hotel, not a pure monument, verify with staff whether non-guests can walk in and view the architecture before counting on entry.

name: Rose Garden, Pushkar
priceNote: free, donations welcome per one source
why: A rose-cultivation garden attraction listed by a couple of tourist-content sites with these hours.
warn: Genuine ambiguity flagged here: Wikipedia's Pushkar article only describes 'rose garden' as a nickname for the town itself (because of its rose cultivation for the local ittar/perfume trade), not a named, gated attraction. It is possible these hours are for a real specific garden this pass could not independently confirm the identity or exact location of, or that tourist-content sites are conflating the town's nickname with a place. Do not build a tight itinerary slot around this without confirming on the ground.

name: Naga Pahar (Nag Pahad) trailhead
priceNote: free, open trail with no gate
why: A mountain in the Aravalli range that forms the natural boundary between Ajmer and Pushkar, tied to a legend about the sage Agastya. The hike from the road to the top is short (about 10 minutes per one source) and rewards with sunrise views and a look down over the Pushkar valley.
warn: Location is genuinely ambiguous - Wikipedia places it between the two towns, and at least one trekking-listing site (AllTrails, 'Maharana Pratap Smarak - Naag Pahad Hike') associates a trailhead of the same name with Anasagar Lake on the Ajmer side, not the Pushkar side. Confirm which trailhead is meant before treating this as a Pushkar-town walk.

name: Ratnagiri (Savitri Mata Temple hill)
priceNote: free; ropeway/temple fees apply separately, see those entries
why: Ratnagiri hill IS the Savitri Mata Temple hill - one source states this directly ('Ratnagiri hill, also known as Savitri Mata Temple Hill'). Not a second stop on top of Savitri Mata Temple, the same climb and the same panorama.
warn: Do not itinerary-plan this as a separate stop from Savitri Mata Temple - it is the same physical location.

name: Pushkar Lake (and the 52 ghats)
priceNote: free to walk/sit; priests on the ghats will ask for a 'donation' - see warn
why: The sacred lake Pushkar exists around, ringed by 52 bathing ghats. Mangala (dawn) aarti runs roughly 5:30-6:00am and Sandhya (evening) aarti roughly 6:30-7:30pm, with a seasonal shift (later in summer, earlier in winter) - no source gives a September-specific time, so treat 6:30-7:00pm as the working estimate.
warn: The ghat-priest 'puja then demand a donation' scam is systemic, not anecdotal - documented across many independent accounts. A man offers flowers, walks you to a ghat, a 'priest' does a short puja, then demands a large sum, escalating with guilt pressure; paying gets a red-yellow thread ('Pushkar Passport') that signals other priests to leave you alone. A firm no and continuing to walk works. Also: photographing people mid-bathing/ritual is not okay; photography is separately banned inside the temples.

name: Brahma Ghat
priceNote: free
why: The most revered of the 52 ghats - believed to be where Brahma performed the yagna that created the lake, marked by a golden-spired shrine.
warn: Shoes off before stepping onto the ghat; same priest-donation scam risk as the lake generally applies here.

name: Varah Ghat
priceNote: free
why: Dedicated to Vishnu's Varaha avatar, ornately carved pillars, a resident priest performs daily puja here. Commonly named as one of the two best ghats to watch the evening aarti from.
warn: Same priest-donation scam risk as the lake generally applies here.

name: Gau Ghat
priceNote: free
why: Named among the 52 ghats and appears in Wikipedia's own ghat list (as 'Gau'), but no source in this pass gave ghat-specific detail beyond the name and its cow-related etymology.
warn: No specific history, aarti role, or visitor detail confirmed for this ghat beyond its name existing.

name: Gandhi Ghat
priceNote: free
why: Commonly described in travel writing as where a portion of Mahatma Gandhi's ashes were immersed - the same claim repeated for a 'Gandhi Ghat' in several other Indian pilgrimage towns.
warn: This specific Pushkar claim is not independently re-verified in this pass and 'Gandhi Ghat' does not appear by that exact name in Wikipedia's own list of Pushkar's named ghats (which instead lists a 'Gobind Ghat' built by Sikhs in memory of Guru Gobind Singh) - there is a real chance of a naming mix-up between the two. Treat the Gandhi-ashes claim as commonly repeated, not confirmed.

name: Gurudwara Singh Sabha
priceNote: free, including langar if served
why: Marks a visit by Guru Nanak Dev, originally called Guru Nanak Dharmasala, now a branch of Sri Guru Singh Sabha Ajmer. Sikh gurudwaras typically run a free community kitchen (langar) and daily prasad distribution.
warn: Exact langar serving times (typically lunch and dinner windows at most gurudwaras) were not found for this specific one in this pass - ask on arrival or call ahead rather than assuming a time.

name: Jain Temple (Golden Temple, Digambar), western shore
priceNote: not found
why: A double-storey Jain temple on Pushkar Lake's western shore, built in 1865, known for a gold-leafed diorama hall - locally nicknamed the Golden Temple.
warn: Opening hours and any entry fee were not found in this pass - the prior research round found no verifiable Jain temple in Pushkar at all, and this round only located the name and a rough description, not logistics. Do not itinerary-plan a specific time slot around this without an on-ground check.

name: Shri Jain Shwetamber Mandir, Ganahera
priceNote: not found
why: A Shwetamber Jain temple listed at Ganahera, in the Pushkar/Ajmer district area - a second named Jain option beyond the lakeside Golden Temple.
warn: Ganahera's exact location relative to Pushkar town center is not confirmed here, and no hours/fee were found - coordinates given are a rough placeholder, not a sourced location.

name: Pushkar Mela Ground (camel/cattle fair ground)
days: Pushkar Camel Fair 2026 runs approximately 17-24 November 2026 (Kartik Purnima, the sacred bathing day, falls on 24 Nov 2026); outside that window the ground itself has no scheduled hours
priceNote: free to walk the ground outside fair dates; fair-time entry/stall pricing not covered here
why: The trading ground and 'slightly derelict-looking stadium' on the outskirts of town, at the foot of the Savitri Mata hill, where the camel and cattle trading and the cultural program happen every November.
warn: A September visit misses the fair by about 2.5 months - the ground will be empty with none of the tent city, trading, or cultural program visible. This is a data point for a November trip, not something worth detouring to see in September.

name: Government-authorized bhang shop
priceNote: not found for Pushkar specifically; a comparable government-authorized shop in Jaisalmer charges roughly INR 150-180 for a bhang lassi/item
why: Government-licensed bhang retail is confirmed to exist in Jaisalmer (beside the fort) and generally in Ajmer, both well documented. This pass found no confirmed, named, licensed bhang shop specifically inside Pushkar town.
warn: Do not assume Pushkar has a formal government shop the way Jaisalmer does - what exists instead, per travel accounts, is Pushkar cafes discreetly selling bhang lassi/cookies as an unofficial 'special' menu item (roughly INR 200-300), which carries more legal and dosage uncertainty than a licensed shop. Confirm legality and location on the ground before treating this as planned.

name: Sadar Bazaar / Sarafa Bazaar
priceNote: free to browse; silver jewellery/mojari/leather/textiles priced per item, bargaining expected - no reliable Pushkar-specific price anchors were found for any category
why: Sadar Bazaar is the main ~1km market strip (pottery, brassware, textiles); Sarafa Bazaar specifically is called out for silver jewellery, ethnic wear, bangles, and mojaris - what Pushkar is actually known for.
warn: Shop hours are a typical-market estimate, not individually source-confirmed per shop. No source gave concrete INR price ranges for silver, mojaris, or leather in Pushkar specifically - get silver hallmark-checked and treat 'gemstones' sold here as decorative, not investment pieces (general Rajasthan market advice, not Pushkar-specific-sourced).

name: Camel safari
priceNote: per person for a 1-2hr ride; half-day (2-3hr), full-day (6-7hr) and overnight (12-14hr) tiers exist but are not itemised in INR by any source found. Anything quoted above roughly INR 1000 for a 1-hour ride is a tourist markup.
why: The signature Pushkar activity - camel-back into the dunes outside town, most popular at sunset for the classic silhouette shot.
warn: Operator-dependent timing, not a fixed schedule. Named operators found (Rajputana Cabs, Pushkar Camel Safari, The Pushkar Route) are self-listed contacts from their own marketing, not independently verified as currently operating - treat as leads to call, not confirmed bookings.

name: Horse safari
priceNote: from roughly INR 550/hr via a booking aggregator (retail/marked-up price, not a confirmed street rate)
why: Marwari-horse rides through the desert/countryside around Pushkar, offered mainly as an add-on by the same operators who run camel safaris.
warn: No named operator with a clean, independently-verified price sheet was found - the figure here comes from a single aggregator listing.

name: Quad biking / ATV desert ride
priceNote: from roughly INR 850/adult
why: Self-driven quad/ATV rides in the dunes, offered standalone or bundled into an evening desert-camp package with folk music and a Rajasthani dinner.
warn: Ride duration for this price tier is a typical-industry estimate (~20-30min), not separately confirmed for Pushkar specifically.

name: Hot air balloon ride
days: mainly runs around the November Camel Fair window; unreliable outside that season
priceNote: per person
why: Aerial flight over Pushkar and the desert, operated by companies like Sky Waltz, timed mainly to the November Camel Fair crowd.
warn: For a September visit specifically: sources are explicit that far fewer operators fly in the April-September window because of the heat, and availability is limited. Do not plan around this as a reliable September booking - confirm directly with the operator before counting on it.

name: Pushkar Yog Shala
priceNote: per drop-in class
why: A beginner/intermediate-friendly yoga school with morning and evening drop-in sessions - the only wellness venue in this dataset with a hard, sourced price attached.
warn: Exact morning/evening class clock-times were not found, only that both slots exist.

name: Pushkar Lake ghat-circuit walk
priceNote: free
why: Walking the main stretch of ghats around the lake - the single best low-cost, high-value activity in Pushkar, works at both sunrise and sunset.
warn: Same ghat-priest donation scam applies here as noted on the Pushkar Lake entry - a firm no and continuing to walk is the reported fix.

name: Old town lanes (around Sadar Bazaar)
priceNote: free beyond whatever is spent
why: Wandering the market lanes around Sadar Bazaar for the town's texture between temple and lake visits - a slow, unstructured filler activity, not a timed sight.
